name: American Resources Corporation

profile.description: American Resources Corporation is an Indiana-based holding company that has moved away from Central Appalachian coal toward critical-mineral recycling and refining. It holds minority stakes in ReElement Technologies (about 17%, rare earth and critical element refining), Willcox International Holdings (about 9%) and Royalty Management Holding (about 8%), and wholly owns Electrified Materials Corporation (magnet and battery recycling). Continuing-operations revenue was $0 in FY2025. Q1 and Q2 2026 10-Qs remain unfiled while its 2025 financials are re-audited, under a Nasdaq exception that runs to November 16, 2026.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): AREC has shifted from coal mining to holding critical-mineral businesses, and affiliate ReElement has begun weekly shipments of high-purity rare earth oxides [3][6]. Because ReElement is now only a ~17% stake, the pivot has not produced revenue for AREC: continuing revenue fell from $39.5M in FY2022 to $0 in FY2025 [2][6]. AI Deployment (0/2): The corporate site and filings mention no AI products or AI-driven savings [6]. Market Share (0/2): AREC's remaining operations are pre-revenue, so it has no category share [2]. Pipeline (1/2): ReElement received air permits in August 2026 for its Marion, Indiana refinery, which targets initial germanium production in Q3 2026 (not yet confirmed in filings) [3][4]. A binding LOI for the ~$13.2M all-stock Blackion acquisition and the Malaysia entity add optionality but no revenue visibility [4]. R&D (0/1): FY2025 R&D was only $107,507 [2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): The website has no formal mission or vision statement. The nearest thing is the CEO's line 'American Resources is deploying a low capex and low operating cost business model', which describes a financial model rather than a purpose [6]. Community Impact (0/2): Reclamation claims of 7,000+ acres of bond releases date from 2019-2020 releases, and no current charitable program or dollar commitment was found [7]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention data was found, and coverage notes possible continuity concerns after management changes [8]. Insider Buying (0/2): 10% holder Golden Properties Ltd. sold roughly 500,000 shares at about $4.07-$4.15 on November 10, 2025, and no open-market insider buys were found [9].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored 2/10 (weighted 2.0 of 10). D/E of 21.7% (1.0) and a forward P/E of 1.52 (1.0) are the only metrics that score; the forward P/E rests on thin analyst estimates for a pre-revenue company [1]. ROE (-290.7% per Yahoo; FMP shows -214.9%), YoY revenue growth (-100%, from $383K in FY2024 to $0 in FY2025), 5-year revenue CAGR (-100% vs. $1.06M in FY2020), profit margin (0%) and a negative forward PEG (-0.22) all score 0 [1][2]. The balance sheet held $72.2M of cash and investments against $8.1M of debt at 12/31/2025, but the prior auditor's opinion on those statements was withdrawn in July 2026 and UHY LLP is re-auditing [2][4]. Liquidity floor cleared: $1.27 x 2,050,088 shares = $2.6M daily [1].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): AREC's businesses process physical feedstock (end-of-life magnets, lithium-ion batteries, coal refuse piles) into rare earth and critical-element products. That chemical and metallurgical work cannot be substituted by AI, and no analyst has cited AI as a risk [3][6]. AI Opportunity (0/1): AREC reports no AI-related revenue; its website and filings do not mention AI [6].

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens AREC looks like a finite player that changes its story to fit the capital markets. It has gone from coal miner to critical-minerals holding company, deconsolidated its main operating affiliate, and now depends on a re-audit and a Nasdaq exception to keep its listing [2][4][6]. The reinvention shows some adaptability, but it was not driven by a stated cause. The withdrawn audit opinion and unfiled 2026 10-Qs point to an organization optimizing for transactions rather than endurance [4].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (0/3): The company offers no mission or cause. Its self-description is a 'low capex and low operating cost business model' with minority stakes across the critical-mineral value chain [6]. Nothing shows a purpose that employees would sacrifice for, beyond the domestic critical-minerals theme the market is currently rewarding.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Auditor GreenGrowth CPAs was dismissed and its opinion on the 2025 statements may not be relied on as of July 13, 2026. Q1 and Q2 2026 10-Qs are late [4]. Commentary flags continuity concerns from management changes [8]. These are signs of organizational strain, not a Circle of Safety.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Management messaging centers on policy tailwinds for onshoring critical minerals and on deal flow (Blackion, the Wyoming County Coal settlement assets) [4]. It does not acknowledge peers such as MP Materials or other refiners as benchmarks to learn from.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): AREC moved from Appalachian coal production to recycling and refining critical minerals. Rather than building the new business itself, it spun the core of that pivot into affiliates it now owns only minority stakes in (ReElement ~17%) [6]. The change reads as opportunistic restructuring rather than a cause-driven reinvention, and AREC itself is left with $0 continuing revenue [2].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Capital allocation has relied on all-stock deals (Blackion, ~$13.2M) and outside financing at affiliates rather than sustained internal investment [4]. Governance lapses around audit reliability suggest leadership has not prioritized the institutional foundations a long-term company needs [4].

investment_thesis: The bull case is optionality on U.S. critical-mineral onshoring. AREC holds stakes in ReElement (~17%), which has begun weekly rare earth oxide shipments, received August 2026 air permits for its Marion, Indiana refinery, and reportedly won a $25M U.S. Department of War award in July 2026 [3][6]. At 12/31/2025 AREC had $72.2M of cash and short-term investments against $8.1M of debt, roughly half its $136M market cap, and the September 2026 $40.0M Wyoming County Coal settlement added West Virginia refuse-pile mineral rights as possible feedstock [2][4]. Analyst targets of $5-$7 compare with a $1.27 share price [4].
thesis_continued: The bear case is about reliability and dilution. The FY2025 net income of $55.4M came entirely from a $73.2M discontinued-operations gain on deconsolidation, while continuing operations lost $17.8M on zero revenue [2]. The prior auditor's 2025 opinion was withdrawn, both 2026 10-Qs are unfiled, and the listing depends on meeting a November 16, 2026 Nasdaq deadline [4]. The stock is down about 73% over a year from a $4.94 high, a 10% holder sold about 500,000 shares in November 2025, and the all-stock Blackion deal plus capital-intensive refining buildouts point to more dilution [1][4][9].
key_catalysts: Filing the re-audited FY2025 10-K and the delinquent Q1/Q2 2026 10-Qs before Nasdaq's November 16, 2026 exception deadline, which would remove the delisting overhang [4]
Confirmation of ReElement's germanium production at the Marion, Indiana campus (targeted Q3 2026) after August 2026 air permits, which would support the value of AREC's ~17% stake [3][6]
Monetizing the West Virginia property, equipment and refuse-pile mineral rights received in the September 2026 $40.0M Wyoming County Coal settlement [4]
key_risks: Delisting risk: failure to file the overdue 10-Qs and the re-audited 2025 financials by November 16, 2026 could cost AREC its Nasdaq listing [4]
Financial statement reliability: GreenGrowth CPAs' opinion on 12/31/2025 statements was withdrawn in July 2026, so the reported $55.4M FY2025 profit and $94.8M equity may be restated [2][4]

Dilution: the ~$13.2M all-stock Blackion acquisition and capital-intensive refining buildouts at affiliates likely require further share issuance, with zero continuing revenue to fund them internally [2][4]
